Reviewed query ownership, cache/freshness and authority guidance against useApiQueryWithSharing and its two session callers. Type erasure is now contained inside the query hook and constrained by its queryFn return type; the free-standing coercer and public sharing option are removed. Common defaults, cancellation and key partitioning are unchanged, so existing contributor guidance remains accurate.

Reviewed the follow-up replacing the free-standing adapter with useApiQueryWithSharing, binding sharing to the queryFn return type. Removed the unused public QueryConfig.structuralSharing option; existing generic call sites remain compatible. The documented session identity/timestamp policy, exports and server semantics are unchanged. Both real-hook identity tests fail individually when their caller stops using sharing, and pass restored. The negative type case rejects Promise<string[]> with TS2322; widening sharing to any triggers the expected unused-directive failure. SDK/UI typechecks and focused source/host-context tests pass. No new device or provider qualification.

Reviewed the documented sessions query result surface against the switch to query-bound sharing. Session summaries, loading/error behavior, keys, polling and identity policy remain unchanged; the internal type correction does not change shipped manual claims or generator inputs.

Traced the recent-work caller through the query-bound sharing hook. Ten-second refresh, captured authority, fetch/normalization and timestamp-only identity reuse are unchanged. Removing sharing only from this caller fails the real Board identity test, restored green. Existing user instructions remain accurate.
